ai.description: Boiga dightoni is a slender, medium-sized snake reaching 1.2 meters. It features a brownish-grey body with dark crossbands and a distinct, triangular-shaped head with large, vertically elliptical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga dightoni* is best distinguished from other Indian cat snakes by its distinct, uniform reddish-brown or brick-red dorsal coloration, which lacks the prominent dark cross-bands or complex patterning seen in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Travancore Cat Snake inhabits moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Travancore Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, often found coiled in tree hollows or foliage during the day to remain camouflaged while it rests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga dightoni* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, though specific clutch size data remains limited.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Travancore Cat Snake is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting moist forests at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
